exposure: Physical activity volume (nil to low, moderate, high)
cohort: Participants from the Queensland Family Cohort study had their physical activity and musculoskeletal symptoms assessed at 24 and 36 weeks' gestation and 6 weeks postpartum.
finding: Nil to low physical activity was associated with greater pelvic organ prolapse severity, but not with urinary incontinence or lumbopelvic pain.
mod_finding: Delivery mode was identified as a predictor for urinary incontinence and pelvic organ prolapse.
